name: MonarchNumberInput
title: NumberInput
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.OutlinedTextField (through MonarchTextField) with KeyboardType.Decimal, and androidx.compose.material3.IconButton for the stepper
summary: A labelled number field that reads and writes numbers in the user's locale, with − and + buttons that step without drift, bounds, helper text and an error state.
whenToUse: For a number the user types or nudges: a quantity, a price, a count of seats.
whenNotToUse: For a value on a continuous range where precision does not matter use the Material 3 Slider. For a code or PIN use MonarchOtpPinInput. For text that only looks numeric, such as a phone number, use MonarchTextField with KeyboardType.Phone.
api: @Composable fun MonarchNumberInput(value: Double?, onValueChange: (Double?) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, label: String? = null, placeholder: String? = null, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, minimum: Double? = null, maximum: Double? = null, step: Double = 1.0, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, showSteppers: Boolean = true, format: ((Double) -> String)? = null, parse: ((String) -> Double?)? = null, labels: MonarchNumberInputLabels = MonarchNumberInputLabels(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
class MonarchNumberInputLabels(increment: String? = null, decrement: String? = null, invalid: String? = null, range: ((minimum: String?, maximum: String?) -> String)? = null)

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or null while the field is empty.

options.name: onValueChange
options.description: Called with the new number, or null when cleared, on every edit that reads as a number, in range or not, and on a step, so a button tapped right after typing reads it; a number out of range is flagged when the field is left, so validate the bounds before saving. The number is rounded to the digits shown.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the field is empty and focused.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error from the app; replaces the field's own messages while present.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest allowed value. Typed values below it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The largest allowed value. Typed values above it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of − or + changes the value, on a grid counted from minimum or 0.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the field and the buttons can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Selectable but not editable; the buttons are disabled.

options.name: showSteppers
options.description: Shows the − and + buttons and the increase and decrease actions.

options.name: format
options.description: Replaces the locale's number format for display. By default up to three fraction digits, or as many as step has.

options.name: parse
options.description: Replaces the reading of the text. Receives non-blank text; returns null when it is not a number.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Increase", "Decrease", "Enter a number." and the range message.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus and press interactions of the field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is null and the placeholder shows while focused. The first step starts from the minimum, or from 0.

states.name: focused
states.description: The outline takes the focus ring color.

states.name: not a number
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter a number." under the field. The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: out of range
states.description: A danger outline and "Enter a number from 0 to 99." under the field. The text is kept and the value is not changed.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the field's own, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The button that would pass the bound is disabled, and its action is removed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The subtle background and the disabled text color; both buttons are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: The text can be selected but not changed; both buttons are disabled.

appearance: The field is MonarchTextField: a surface fill with the input border, the focus ring color when focused and the danger strong color in error. The − and + signs use the default text color, or the disabled text color when their button is disabled. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same behavior as the web: the text is read in the locale's conventions (grouping and decimal separators, the locale's own digits, currency signs and a percent sign around the number, accounting negatives), unreadable or out-of-range text is kept, flagged and never saved, and steps move to the next point on the step grid in decimal arithmetic. iOS uses the system TextField(value:format:), which puts unreadable text back, and the system Stepper. The web's arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down and largeStep have no touch equivalent and are not offered; TalkBack users get Increase and Decrease custom actions on the field instead of a spinbutton role, which Android does not have. The web's formatOptions (Intl.NumberFormat) are replaced by the format and parse lambdas, so percent and currency styles are the app's java.text.NumberFormat; there is no percent mode that divides by 100. The web's sm, md and lg sizes are not offered; the field is the size of MonarchTextField. The buttons do not repeat while held. The keyboard is KeyboardType.Decimal; Compose has no signed number keyboard, so whether a minus key is shown depends on the keyboard app.
accessibility: The field is the Material 3 text field: TalkBack reads the label, the text and the error.
A new message for unreadable or out-of-range text is the field's error, shown with text and a danger outline, not color alone.
The − and + buttons are Material 3 icon buttons named "Decrease" and "Increase", each with a 48dp touch target; the sign itself is hidden from TalkBack.
The field has Increase and Decrease custom actions while a step is possible, so TalkBack users can step without leaving the field.
The decrease button is at the start and the increase button at the end, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
A disabled or read-only field disables both buttons.
edgeCases: Changing value from outside replaces the text on screen and clears the field's own message.
A typed value with more digits than shown is rounded half up to the digits shown when it is saved.
A step from text that cannot be read starts from the last saved value.
A step of zero or less does not move the value.

examples.title: In a Field with limits
examples.template:
MonarchNumberInput(
    value = seats,
    onValueChange = { seats = it },
    label = {{label}},
    helperText = {{description}},
    minimum = {{min|double}},
    maximum = {{max|double}},
)
examples.code:
MonarchNumberInput(
    value = seats,
    onValueChange = { seats = it },
    label = "Seats",
    helperText = "Between 1 and 50.",
    minimum = 1.0,
    maximum = 50.0,
)

examples.title: A decimal step without drift
examples.code:
MonarchNumberInput(
    value = price,
    onValueChange = { price = it },
    label = "Price",
    step = 0.1,
    placeholder = "0",
)

examples.title: A currency format
examples.setup:
val currency = remember { java.text.NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance(java.util.Locale.US) }
var amount by remember { mutableStateOf<Double?>(12.5) }
examples.code:
MonarchNumberInput(
    value = amount,
    onValueChange = { amount = it },
    label = "Amount",
    step = 0.01,
    format = { currency.format(it) },
    parse = { text -> runCatching { currency.parse(text)?.toDouble() }.getOrNull() },
)
